sections.content:
32,170 people

were counted on the census as "musicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Musicians write, arrange, orchestrate, conduct and perform musical compositions.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "musicians", 14.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "musicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "musicians" included:

  • social and humanities scientists
  • civil engineers
  • newspaper and periodical broadcast journalists and reporters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "musicians" there were more men than women (72.1% compared with 27.9%).

This means "musicians" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 72.1% and women made up 27.9% of "musicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "musicians" included:

  • managers in logistics
  • pre-press technicians
  • rail travel assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "musicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "musicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "musicians", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (60.9% compared with 39.1%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (83.4%) than an employee (16.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Lewisham, this is in the same region of London.
